result.title: TesseraFlow: Scalable Video Diffusion for Dynamic Medical Imaging Inverse Problems
result.summary: Generative priors are state-of-the-art for modeling medical images in image reconstruction tasks, but reconstruction with video priors takes tens of seconds to minutes per frame. Latent priors inherit the errors of their autoencoder, the memory of pixel-space whole-frame priors grows with the frame size, and pixel-space patch priors are slow for two reasons. First, their deep networks process every frame at full resolution at every sampling step, even though early steps resolve only low frequencies. Second, their samplers spend many network evaluations per sampling step on overlapping windows, multiple re-noising rounds, or backpropagation through the prior. We introduce TesseraFlow, a complex-valued pixel-space flow prior that reduces the first cost. A global encoder reads a low-resolution view of every frame once per sampling step. A single shallow decoder operates on this view during early steps and on full-resolution space-time tiles during later steps, so no network processes a whole frame at full resolution. Our sampler, ReTile, addresses the second reason. We use randomized grid shifting at every sampling step along with re-noising, which acts as a stochastic gradient instead of computing overlapping tiles, so a single network pass per sampling step suffices. On its own, ReTile speeds up an existing global-context patch prior by 6-9x, and our prior adds a further 3-5x speedup. TesseraFlow reconstructs about one 256x256 frame per second, 20-367x faster than patch and latent video priors, and can match or exceed the best generative baseline on cardiac, brain, and abdominal MRI and lung CT, at a fraction of its GPU time.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TesseraFlow，一种用于动态医学影像反问题重建的复数像素空间 flow 先验：全局编码器每步只读低分辨率视图，浅解码器在早期步骤用该视图、后期改用全分辨率时空 tile，配合随机网格平移与 re-noising 的 ReTile 采样器，大幅降低每帧 GPU 时间。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作本身是医学图像重建而非视觉推理，但其「早期步骤只做低分辨率计算、后期再细化」的分阶段算力分配可能可供核查 LVR 中动态计算预算与粗到细状态更新的设计。
